how: The container was enrolled (device ad64617c-b1e8-465f-ac65-4c780082cc18, name bulut, platform cloud) and connected to the broker (session c044c3fc..., 18:19:50Z). While `docker stats` was sampled every second for 90 s, Chromium was launched INSIDE the container (docker exec, Playwright 1.62.0, headless) and taken to three public pages (example.com, wikipedia.org, hetzner.com) with 8 s on each, then closed. Idle = the worker without a browser open.
not_the_broker_path: The three navigations were driven directly in the container, not as browser.* commands through the broker: a device command needs an owner session, which the lead does not hold. The memory of Chromium on this host is the same either way; the worker's own overhead per command is not in this number.
device_alias: bulut (devices.metadata_json.aliases, written 2026-09-30 by the lead, delegated by the owner)
conclusion: 0.65 GB peak for three pages against a 2 GB cap on a host with 4.5 GB free: CPX32 holds the cloud worker at this concurrency. The blue-green switch (two api colours at once, ~1.4 GB each) plus this worker was not measured together; the next release does that measurement.

earlier.2026-09-30 (cycle pilot-02): NOT_RUN on the home PC: the Docker engine was not running; the estimate then was 0.5-1 GB idle from blog sources.
